Investigate moving the CineJoy streaming proxy directly onto the LG webOS 8.5 TV (LG 32LR686BPSA, webOS platform 23, firmware 13.50.44), evaluate three architectural approaches, implement an isolated standalone Proof of Concept (PoC) webOS JS service compatible with on-device Node.js 12.22.2, and deliver a comprehensive technical feasibility report comparing all approaches.

Working directory: /home/prem/webos-projects/cinejoy-webos
Integrity mode: development

Target device specification:
- Model: LG 32LR686BPSA
- Platform: LG webOS 23 (webOS 8.5.0)
- Firmware: 13.50.44
- TV IP: 192.168.1.15 (SSH port 9922, user prisoner, key /home/prem/.ssh/lg-tv_webos_decrypted)
- Native On-Device Runtime: Linux 5.4.96 aarch64, Node.js v12.22.2, Chromium ~108 (WAM)
- Total Device Memory: 1349 MB RAM (~340 MB available under normal TV OS load)

## Requirements

### R1. Architecture & Upstream Constraint Analysis (Approach 1)
Analyze the existing proxy implementation (server/index.js, server/resolver.js, server/hls-proxy.js, server/crush.wasm) and empirically evaluate Approach 1 (Direct TV frontend communication). Determine whether client-side webOS Chromium can directly resolve and stream media without an intermediary proxy by evaluating:
- W3C Forbidden Header constraints (Origin / Referer) on browser fetch() and HTMLMediaElement <video>.
- Upstream CDN response behavior (e.g. lightspeed.st, nebula) when requests lack Referer: https://cinejoy.pk/.
- Client-side WebAssembly execution (crush.wasm) and Web Cryptography API (AES-256-GCM) feasibility within the TV browser sandbox.

### R2. Isolated Proof-of-Concept Package (Approach 2 & 3)
Build a completely separate, standalone webOS test application and JS Service (e.g., App ID com.cinejoy.poc, Service ID com.cinejoy.poc.service) without modifying the working com.cinejoy.tv production code.
- Ensure 100% strict compatibility with the TV's native Node.js v12.22.2 runtime (no optional chaining ?., no nullish coalescing ??, no numeric separators _, replace global fetch / AbortSignal.timeout with Node 12 HTTP/HTTPS streams or bundled polyfills).
- Package crush.wasm and implement cryptographic stream resolution and M3U8 manifest URL rewriting within the service.
- Implement a lightweight local HTTP streaming server inside the JS service binding strictly to 127.0.0.1.
- Implement zero-buffering HTTP range streaming (HTTP 206 Partial Content) and client disconnection cleanup.
- Package into a deployable .ipk using ares-package.

### R3. On-Device TV Verification & Lifecycle Investigation
Deploy the PoC IPK to the physical TV via Developer Mode (ares-install) and empirically test:
- Service launch mechanisms: Test launch via PalmServiceBridge / WebOSServiceBridge (luna://com.cinejoy.poc.service/start) and direct process lifecycle.
- Localhost HTTP binding: Verify com.cinejoy.poc Chromium frontend can fetch from http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/...
- Media streaming & playback: Load an adaptive HLS video stream through the on-device localhost proxy into an HTML5 <video> element. Verify seeking forward/backward, playback event progression (loadstart, canplay, playing), and buffer health.
- Service persistence & watchdog: Measure whether webOS ls-hubd or the OS activity manager terminates the background Node service during active playback, pause, or idle states.
- Memory & CPU profiling: Monitor memory usage on the physical TV (free -m, /proc/<pid>/status, RSS) during prolonged playback to verify TV RAM remains within safe limits (under 50 MB RSS for service).

### R4. Technical Feasibility Report & Migration Recommendation
Deliver a structured technical feasibility report comparing:
1. Approach 1: Direct client communication (eliminating proxy).
2. Approach 2: Pure Luna bus service (passing binary video segments or base64 over Luna IPC).
3. Approach 3: Embedded local HTTP server hosted by webOS JS service on 127.0.0.1.
Recommend the optimal architecture that completely eliminates the laptop dependency while maintaining zero regression, and provide a verified rollback and migration plan.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Feasibility & Constraints
- [ ] Empirical proof documenting why upstream video CDNs accept or reject direct browser requests without proxy headers.
- [ ] Full compatibility audit of proxy logic against Node.js 12.22.2 completed with all incompatible syntax/APIs replaced.

### Standalone PoC Deployment
- [ ] Separate PoC package (com.cinejoy.poc) builds without errors and installs onto the physical TV (192.168.1.15) via ares-install.
- [ ] Existing com.cinejoy.tv app and laptop proxy remain completely untouched and fully functional.

### On-Device TV Verification
- [ ] Service successfully starts on the physical TV and binds an HTTP server to 127.0.0.1.
- [ ] Frontend on the TV connects to the on-device localhost proxy and resolves streams autonomously without contacting the laptop (192.168.1.6).
- [ ] Video playback starts, buffers, and plays smoothly on the TV with active seeking tested.
- [ ] Service lifecycle tested: verified whether the service remains alive throughout continuous playback.
- [ ] Physical memory impact verified on TV (RSS, total free memory).

### Report & Migration Plan
- [ ] Comprehensive technical feasibility report comparing all three approaches across memory, latency, playback stability, and webOS lifecycle rules.
- [ ] Clear recommendation and low-risk migration strategy for CineJoy.

1. **Physical TV Developer Mode Lifetime**: Developer Mode on webOS displays a countdown timer (typically 50–1000 hours depending on Developer Mode app refresh).
